A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Diffusion Bridge Implicit Models. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and matchable despite added material and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original DBIM experiments on image translation and ImageNet inpainting, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and reconstruction/interpolation examples.

after.justification: v4 retains original DBIM experiments and additionally reports measured runtimes and quantitative generation-diversity results in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The non-Markovian bridge construction, training objective, sampling updates, booting-noise initialization and high-order solvers are retained. Appendix E's algorithm is unchanged; expanded explanations do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Edges-to-Handbags at 64×64, DIODE-Outdoor translation at 256×256, and ImageNet inpainting at 256×256 with a 128×128 center mask. The added analyses reuse these task conditions.

E2.justification: Rectified Flow is removed from the image-translation comparison in Table 2. Other existing comparator identities remain; the additional I2SB rows in Table 3 extend its sampling budgets rather than introduce a new baseline.

E3.justification: The reported training settings, evaluation splits and existing sampler schedules are retained. Added protocols measure runtime on an A100 with batch size 16 and diversity using five generations for each of 1,000 conditions. Table 3 also adds I2SB evaluations at 10 and 20 NFE.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds direct runtime-versus-NFE analysis and quantitative diversity comparisons across stochasticity levels and sampling budgets, substantially extending scrutiny of two central claims. v4 also adds an explicit high-NFE failure-case discussion and illustration, while retaining the original stochasticity and solver-order ablations.

E5.justification: v4 newly reports runtime means and standard deviations, describing measurements over eight batches with the first discarded. v2 contains no corresponding uncertainty reporting. Quality metrics still lack repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 8–9 introduce previously unreported runtime and diversity outcomes, including higher diversity scores for eta=0 than eta=1 at every listed NFE. Existing scores also change: Table 4's ImageNet FID at eta=0 and 10 NFE changes from 4.62 to 4.51. Additional low-NFE I2SB and DBIM results appear in Table 3; these revisions do not establish a method change.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 corrects Equation (50) by restoring conditioning on x_tn and the missing negative x_tn term in the gradient expansion. The resulting Markovian condition, principal propositions, proofs and high-order derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain training-free DDBM acceleration up to 25×, preservation of marginals and training objectives, high-order solver extensions, and booting-noise-enabled reconstruction and interpolation. The added evidence supports these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds concrete limitations concerning real-time suitability, dependence on pretrained-model capability, and persistent face/hand artifacts. It also qualifies comparisons with task-agnostic methods and notes that sharper images may inflate the diversity score. The original interpretations of stochasticity and high-order sampling are largely retained.

D1.justification: v4 supplies hardware, batch size, CUDA timing functions, warm-up handling and diversity-computation details for the new analyses. The stated code access path changes from thu-ml/DBIM to thu-ml/DiffusionBridge. Existing model parameterizations, training budgets and sampling instructions are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands positioning against directly relevant implicit-sampling predecessors, including BBDM, I3SB and SinSR, distinguishing DBIM's broader DDBM framework and high-order solvers. It also adds context on generalized and discrete implicit sampling, accelerated inverse problems, stochastic interpolants and consistency bridge distillation.

P1.justification: Parts of the introduction and related-work discussion are rewritten, a short main-text Related Work section is inserted, and new limitations and supplementary-results sections are added. Most existing exposition and section ordering remain intact; notation, cross-references and publication headers receive localized edits.

P2.justification: v4 adds runtime and diversity Tables 8–9 and failure-case Figure 5, shades and reorganizes comparison rows, and expands Table 3. Table 5 and Figure 4 move, while existing schematics and sample grids are retained; the sample appendix moves from G to H.

improvement.justification: v4 better supports existing efficiency and diversity claims through Appendix G, clarifies relationships to prior implicit-bridge methods, states concrete limitations, and corrects Equation (50). These improve evidential support and transparency. However, revised translation scores introduce inconsistencies: Table 2 retains a Handbags FID of 1.74 at 20 NFE while Tables 5–6 report 1.76. The net improvement is therefore useful but limited.
